abstract: Maintains antenna pedestal drive mechanisms, emergency slew capabilities, and motion latency records
system_message:
You are Antenna systems engineer (ANT). The Antenna systems engineer (ANT) maintains antenna pedestal drive mechanisms, emergency slew capabilities, and motion latency records, as well as tracking structural wind loading assessments for ground station antenna radomes and pedestal mounts.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains antenna pedestal drive mechanisms, emergency slew capabilities, and motion latency records（SLEW）
information_points.content:
ANT-SLEW-J4Y：For the Mid-latitude dual-reflector earth station, the primary azimuth-elevation tracking pedestal has its emergency fast-slew drive enabled according to the drive mechanism commissioning log, with an emergency slew transition latency of 60 s recorded during the 180-degree azimuth emergency turnaround drill.
ANT-SLEW-GT4：For the Equatorial high-elevation tracking complex, the drive mechanism commissioning log indicates that the emergency fast-slew drive is enabled on the primary azimuth-elevation tracking pedestal, while pedestal calibration testing recorded an emergency slew transition latency of 35 s during the 180-degree azimuth turnaround drill.
ANT-SLEW-M6D：For the Polar orbit dedicated tracking facility, the primary azimuth-elevation tracking pedestal drive mechanism commissioning log confirms that the emergency fast-slew drive is enabled, and pedestal motion calibration testing during a 180-degree azimuth emergency turnaround drill measured an emergency slew transition latency of 25 s.

information_points.title: Structural wind loading（WIND）
information_points.content:
ANT-WIND-EUY：The antenna radome and pedestal mount of the Equatorial high-elevation tracking complex hold a certified survival gust speed rating of 160 km/h based on structural wind survivability records.
ANT-WIND-LKQ：According to the structural wind survivability certificate, the antenna radome and pedestal mount of the Polar orbit dedicated tracking facility have a survival gust speed rating of 180 km/h.
ANT-WIND-ZKT：The structural wind survivability certificate indicates that the Mid-latitude dual-reflector earth station has a survival gust speed rating of 140 km/h across its antenna radome and pedestal mount.
